PV02-q01-g71gpi: Waiting until someone breaks a rule invites trouble; explain the rules at the start of the trip.
Explain the rules at the start of the trip, not later, to help avoid trouble.
PV02-q02-myikhs: Being late does not change the rule: wait for riders to sit down or brace themselves.
Riders can stumble when the bus starts; wait until they sit down or brace themselves.
PV02-q03-r0s17a: Never let a disruptive rider off where it would be unsafe for them; you must keep them safe too.
A dark, empty spot is unsafe; a well-lit area with other people or the next scheduled stop may be safer.
PV02-q04-q1e2xx: The handbook names intersections, not straight highways, as where bus accidents often happen.
Weather is not the point here; bus accidents often happen at intersections, even with signals or stop signs.
PV02-q05-bpwx6x: The handbook's warning for pulling out is clipping mirrors or striking passing cars, not rolling over.
Air pressure is not the issue; buses leaving stops can scrape mirrors or hit passing vehicles.
PV02-q06-eihopv: Never assume other drivers will brake to make room; wait for the gap to open.
Pulling out slowly still assumes others will react; wait for a gap big enough to speed up and merge.
PV02-q07-f0acd8: Even in good weather, the posted curve speed is set for cars and may be too fast for many buses.
A posted curve speed is not a minimum; it is set for cars and may be too fast for a bus.
PV02-q08-a90hch: Good traction does not make you safe; a bus going too fast with good traction may roll over.
Sliding off is what happens with poor traction; with good traction the bus may roll over.
PV02-q09-bj9an6: Leaning outward is a sign of your own speed, not of the curve's design speed.
Tire pressure is not the cause the handbook gives; leaning outward means you are going too fast.
PV02-q10-n7n8xz: Backwards: convex mirrors make things look smaller and farther away, so they are really closer.
Convex mirrors do not show true distance; things look smaller and farther away than they are.
PV02-q11-oh4dmn: At least 50 feet is the drawbridge rule; at a railroad crossing stop between 15 and 50 feet.
Stopping as close as you can breaks the rule; stop between 15 and 50 feet before the crossing.
PV02-q12-dcfhtz: Gates are not the reason; open the forward door if it helps you see or hear a train.
Transmission type does not matter; open the forward door if it helps you see or hear a train.
PV02-q13-gtwb2y: With a manual transmission, never change gears while crossing the tracks, not even to downshift.
Never change gears while crossing; a missed shift can stall the bus on the tracks.
PV02-q14-wvowkl: After a train passes, you still must check that no other train is coming on the other tracks.
Poor view down the tracks is a reason for more care, not one of the no-stop cases.
PV02-q15-93jx6l: A streetcar crossing is one of the cases where you slow down and check instead of stopping.
A crossing marked "exempt" is one of the cases where you slow down and check instead of stopping.
PV02-q16-nwkwqf: 15 to 50 feet is the railroad crossing rule; at a drawbridge stop at least 50 feet before the draw.
With no signal light or attendant you must stop, then make sure the draw is completely closed.
PV02-q17-aq76gz: Empty roads are not a no-stop case; only a green light or an attendant or traffic officer is.
Seeing the far side is not a no-stop case; only a green light or an attendant or traffic officer is.
PV02-q18-0yrkng: Interstate drivers write a report for each bus; if there are no defects, the report says so.
The report must name the bus and list defects, or say there are none; the bus number alone is not enough.
PV02-q19-y31949: Fueling with no riders aboard is not prohibited; the ban is fueling in a closed building with riders aboard.
Explaining trip rules at the start is what the handbook tells you to do.
PV02-q20-rknddd: Towing with riders aboard is allowed only to the nearest safe spot to let them off, not to the garage.
When getting off would be unsafe, towing is allowed, but only to the nearest safe spot.
PV02-q21-1ddw1g: The interlock does more than warn: it puts on the brakes and holds the throttle at idle.
It is not the parking brake; it releases on its own when the rear door closes.
PV02-q22-x0ihph: The interlock releases when you close the rear door.
The interlock is not a parking brake, and the rear door does not have to be open to park.
